This gives the complete support graph; an absorbing recurrent class is precisely one of its terminal strongly connected components. A separate exact reproduction tested each ordered pair of colorings on every connected labeled mask at orders 2–5 and used Tarjan components and a cycle-length gcd. It returned the largest-component distributions {2:1}, {1:1,2:3}, {1:12,2:26}, {1:188,2:405,4:135}, and exactly one size-four class of period two in each exceptional graph, with the asserted canonical orbit counts {59:60,221:60,495:15}. The sufficient partition inequalities force both blocks to exchange colors regardless of the hub and keep the hub tied. Both next states in the opposite phase are supported; alternation excludes odd returns and a two-step return is possible. Fair independent tie-breaking gives the stated uniform stationary law. Nondegenerate independent biases preserve support. Replay the finite census with the mask and support construction in RESULT.md lines 34–55, canonicalizing over every permutation and testing each exceptional component for a two-step return and no edge within a phase. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its advertised Python 3.8 minimum is inaccurate for its int.bit_count usage, which needs Python 3.10 or later. value.rationale: The scientific question is the first appearance and structure of persistent randomness in a natural majority model, not merely a trivial enumeration of small graphs. In particular, the strict-margin two-block criterion is a reusable graph-local test at arbitrary order: it produces a four-state communicating class with genuine coin-toss branching but a two-round temporal period. The independently repeated core census is not counted as a distinct contribution or used to overcome the originality failure.
